Roadmaps.magicalStriker: Either a scattering of innate spells, or prepared or spontaneous spells with a rank up to one less than half the creature's level, rounded up.
Roadmaps.skillParagon: Many skills, potentially one or two of them extreme. At least one special ability uses the creature's skills in combat.
Roadmaps.sniper: Melee Strikes are weaker than ranged Strikes.
Roadmaps.soldier: Reactive Strike or other tactical abilities.
Roadmaps.spellcaster: Prepared or spontaneous spells with a rank of up to half the creature's level, rounded up.
Roadmaps.alchemist: High Crafting. Abilities: infused alchemical items, Quick Bomber if a bomber alchemist, a few other alchemist abilities.
Roadmaps.barbarian: High Athletics. Abilities: Rage, instinct ability and related feats, raging resistance.
Roadmaps.bard: Moderate Occultism, high Performance, high Charisma-based skills. Abilities: spontaneous occult spellcasting as a bard of their level, composition spells, muse feats.
Roadmaps.champion: Moderate Religion. Abilities: Blessing of the devoted and related feats, cause, champion's aura, devotion spells, exalted reaction, Shield Block, Smite.
Roadmaps.clericCloistered: High Religion, moderate or high skill themed to deity. Abilities: prepared divine spellcasting as a cleric of their level; divine font; domain spells.
Roadmaps.clericWarpriest: Moderate Religion, moderate or high skill themed to deity. Abilities: prepared divine spellcasting as a cleric of their level; divine font, Shield Block.
Roadmaps.druid: High Nature, moderate or high skill from order. Abilities: prepared primal spellcasting as a druid of their level; order ability, order feats, and order spell; Shield Block.
Roadmaps.fighter: High Acrobatics or Athletics. Abilities: Bravery, Reactive Strike, Shield Block, a few fighter abilities and feats associated with a combat style.
Roadmaps.investigator: High Society, high methodology skill, plus more skills than usual. Abilities: Pursue a Lead, Devise a Stratagem, methodology action.
Roadmaps.monk: High Acrobatics, Athletics, or both. Abilities: Flurry of Blows, metal strikes, mystic strikes, perfected form, stance and related feats, qi abilities.
Roadmaps.oracle: High Religion, high mystery skill, moderate or high skill themed to deity. Abilities: spontaneous divine spellcasting as an oracle of their level; oracle mystery and related spells, revelation spells, curse.
Roadmaps.ranger: Moderate Nature and moderate to high Survival. Abilities: Hunt Prey, hunter's edge, nature's edge, masterful hunter, swift prey, companion or combat style. Hunt Prey is optional for a simpler ranger.
Roadmaps.rogue: High Stealth and Thievery, plus more skills than usual. Abilities: sneak attack, surprise attack, deny advantage, debilitating strike, master strike, rogue's racket.
Roadmaps.sorcerer: Moderate bloodline skills and high Charisma-based bloodline skills. Abilities: spontaneous spellcasting of a tradition based on bloodline as a sorcerer of their level, bloodline and related feats and spells.
Roadmaps.swashbuckler: High Acrobatics, plus high style skill. Abilities: confident finisher, panache, precise strike, stylish combatant, swashbuckler's style.
Roadmaps.witch: High patron skill. Abilities: prepared spellcasting of a tradition based on patron as a witch of their level, familiar, witch's patron and related cantrip, hex, and spells.
Roadmaps.wizard: High Arcana. Abilities: prepared arcane spellcasting as a wizard of their level, Drain Bonded Item, school spell, and curriculum spells.

TraitNotes.angel: Aura: each angel has a unique aura based on its role as a messenger. Rituals: usually angelic messenger (Monster Core).
TraitNotes.archon: Virtue Ability: archons each represent a specific virtue, like courage or hope, and have a special ability based on it.
TraitNotes.azata: Freedom Ability: azatas each represent a specific freedom, like free expression or free love, and have a special ability based on it.
TraitNotes.celestial: Saves: often a +1 status bonus to all saves vs. magic. Strikes: typically have the holy trait.
TraitNotes.construct: Many constructs lack minds and have the mindless trait. If mindless, add mental immunity.
TraitNotes.daemon: Languages: telepathy 100 feet. Death Ability: daemons each represent a specific kind of death and have a special ability based on it.
TraitNotes.demon: Languages: telepathy, usually reaching 100 feet. HP is typically high to account for multiple weaknesses. Sin Vulnerability and Sin Ability based on the sin represented. Divine Innate Spells: usually 5th-rank translocate and at-will 4th-rank translocate. Rituals: usually demonic pact (Monster Core).
TraitNotes.devil: Languages: telepathy, usually reaching 100 feet. Divine Innate Spells: usually one 5th-rank translocate and at-will 4th-rank translocate. Rituals: usually diabolic pact (Monster Core). Infernal Hierarchy Ability based on the role in the infernal hierarchy.
TraitNotes.dragon: Dragon Breath: many dragons have an activity that exhales damaging magical energy, and the dragon's theme sets the details.
TraitNotes.fiend: Saves: often a +1 status bonus to all saves vs. magic. Strikes: typically have the unholy trait.
TraitNotes.fire: Weaknesses: typically cold and water; only cold is applied because creatures typically have at most one weakness. Strikes: typically deal fire damage.
TraitNotes.fungus: Fungi without minds have the mindless trait. If mindless, add mental immunity. Weaknesses: sometimes slashing or fire.
TraitNotes.incorporeal: Resistances: all damage except force, ghost touch, vitality for undead, or spirit; double resistance vs. non-magical. Strikes: magical trait, typically low or moderate damage. HP is terrible at lower levels, then low at higher levels. AC is typically low or moderate.
TraitNotes.ooze: Almost all oozes lack minds and have the mindless trait. Add mental immunity. With no vision, add visual effects immunity. AC is usually terrible, and HP is usually around double.
TraitNotes.plant: Plants without minds have the mindless trait. If mindless, add mental immunity. Weaknesses: sometimes fire.
TraitNotes.protean: Resistances: protean anatomy (Monster Core). Divine Innate Spells: constant unfettered movement. Change Shape (Monster Core).
TraitNotes.swarm: Size is based on the entire mass, usually Large or bigger. Weaknesses: area damage and splash damage; only area damage is applied. Resistances: usually one physical type has lower or no resistance.
TraitNotes.undead: Almost all undead are unholy. Ghostly undead have the incorporeal trait. Undead without minds have the mindless trait, so add mental immunity. HP: void healing (Monster Core). Add unconscious immunity instead of sleep if it never rests.
TraitNotes.wood: Weaknesses: fire and axes or slashing; only fire is applied.

Rules.needsWeakness: The creature has an extreme statistic, or four or more high ones, with nothing low. Add a low statistic to offset them.
Rules.tooManyExtremes: The creature has {count} extreme statistics at level {level}. Creatures of this level typically have up to {allowed}.
Rules.noLowStatistic: The creature has high statistics but nothing low. Lower at least one statistic.
Rules.noHighStatistic: The creature has low statistics but nothing high. Raise at least one statistic.
Rules.extremeWithoutLow: An extreme statistic at level {level} needs at least {count} low statistics to offset it.
Rules.allHighDefenses: AC and every save are high. Lower at least one save.
Rules.manyHighDefenses: {count} of the 4 defenses, AC and the saves, are high, with none low. Lower one of them.
Rules.earlyExtremeArmorClass: Extreme AC at level {level} makes the creature very hard for the party to hit. Use high AC at low levels.
Rules.aboveScale: {statistic} is above the extreme value for level {level}.
Rules.belowScale: {statistic} is below the lowest value for level {level}.
Rules.oozeArmorClass: Oozes have low AC, so their AC should not be higher than low.
Rules.swarmHitPoints: Swarms have low HP, so their HP should not be higher than moderate.
Rules.missingTrait: The {trait} trait usually comes with the {required} trait.
Rules.missingWeakness: The {trait} trait usually comes with a weakness to {required}.
Rules.missingProtection: The {trait} trait usually comes with immunity or resistance to {required}.
Rules.rangedStrikeDamage: {name} is a ranged Strike with extreme damage. Ranged Strikes should deal high damage at most.
Rules.extremeArmorClassHitPoints: Extreme AC together with high HP makes the creature too hard to bring down. Lower its HP or AC.
Rules.multipleExtremeSaves: The creature has {count} extreme saves. Almost no creature should have more than one, even at high levels.
Rules.linkedExtremeStrike: {name} has an extreme attack bonus or damage together with a high value in the other, so every attack is strong on both counts.
Rules.agileStrikeDamage: {name} is agile, so its damage should typically be moderate.
Rules.earlyExtremeSpells: Extreme spell numbers are standard from level 15. At level {level} they suit only creatures with very weak defenses.
Rules.perceptionWisdom: The creature has high Perception with a low Wisdom modifier. Perception should follow Wisdom unless the creature has acute senses.
Rules.skillAttribute: {skill} is high while {attribute} is low. A creature's best skills should go with its best attribute modifiers.
Rules.tooManyHighSkills: The creature has {count} high skills. Most creatures have no more than three.
Rules.tooManyWeaknesses: The creature has {count} weaknesses. Creatures typically have at most one.
Rules.weaknessHitPoints: A weakness calls for extra HP, but this creature has low HP.
Rules.broadResistanceHitPoints: A broad resistance usually comes with fewer HP, but this creature has high HP.
Rules.sizeForLevel: {size} creatures are seldom found at level {level}.
Rules.extremeStrengthSize: An extreme Strength modifier at level {level} is usually reserved for {size} or larger creatures.
Rules.flyingStrikers: A flying creature with ranged Strikes is typically introduced around level 7, when PCs gain flight. This one is level {level}.
Rules.traitAttribute: The {trait} trait expects a different {attribute} modifier.
